title: The 14th Annual Halloween Spooktacular!
summary: The 14th annual Halloween Spooktacular of Stuff You Should Know, an ad-free episode in which Josh and Chuck read two public domain scary short stories aloud in character. The first is H.G. Wells' "The Red Room," about a visitor who spends a night in a haunted room in a castle, where candles keep going out and he is left terrified and knocked unconscious; the three old servants tell him fear itself haunts the room. The second is J.D. Beresford's "The Misanthrope," narrated by a visitor to a remote island who befriends a hermit, William Copley, who cannot bear being looked at over the shoulder, since he sees people's vices and distorted true selves when he does so. The episode closes with the hosts' sign-off and remarks about their Halloween tradition.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts welcome listeners to the Halloween Spooktacular and joke about Chuck's failed attempt to channel Megal.

segments.title: Halloween tradition overview
segments.summary: Hosts explain their yearly tradition of reading public domain scary short stories, and agree on which story goes first.

segments.title: Introducing H.G. Wells
segments.summary: Chuck introduces H.G. Wells as author of The Time Machine and a scary story, The Red Room, and the hosts set up their reading roles.

segments.title: The Red Room, part one: the three old servants
segments.summary: A visitor arrives at a castle and talks with three old servants, a man with a withered arm, a man with a shade over his eyes, and an old woman, who warn him about the haunted red room. He insists on going.

segments.title: The Red Room, part two: entering the room and discussion
segments.summary: The narrator walks the passage to the red room, locks himself in, and checks the room. The hosts discuss the story's setup, the earlier death of the young duke, and the legend of the wife.

segments.title: The Red Room, part three: lighting candles
segments.summary: The narrator lights seventeen candles to banish darkness, then candles begin going out one by one while he struggles with matches.

segments.title: The Red Room, part four: darkness and ending
segments.summary: The last candles are extinguished, the narrator screams and collides with furniture, and wakes in daylight bandaged. The old man says the room holds fear itself. The hosts praise the story and Wells.

segments.title: Transition to second story
segments.summary: Hosts take a message break reference and introduce the second story by J.D. Beresford.

segments.title: Introducing The Misanthrope
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck describe the common pattern of rational visitors investigating creepy places and set up roles for the reading.

segments.title: The Misanthrope, part one: the visitor sails to the rock
segments.summary: The narrator recounts that a hermit has lived on the Golden Rock off Trevone for a winter, and that he secretly decides to visit him by boat.

segments.title: The Misanthrope, part two: meeting William Copley
segments.summary: The narrator meets William Copley, who insists on going behind the narrator and never turns his back on him. They fish together and the narrator stays the night.

segments.title: The Misanthrope, part three: Copley's confession
segments.summary: Copley explains his lifelong condition: when he looks at people over his shoulder he sees their vices and distorted true selves. He describes his brother Claude, his housemaster, his engagement to Helen, and why he withdrew from people.

segments.title: The Misanthrope ending
segments.summary: The next morning Copley looks back at the narrator over his shoulder and shows a look of disgust, leaving the narrator unsure what he saw. The hosts discuss the ending.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up the Halloween Spooktacular and sign off with a wish to stay safe and be ghoulish.

segments.title: Production credit
segments.summary: Closing production credit for iHeartRadio and where to find more podcasts.
